title: Load balancer failure with health checks
question: How many failed requests do health checks prevent when Server B crashes?
description: Same scenario as the baseline with one change: the load balancer probes each backend every 5 s and removes it after two failed probes. Compare it with the baseline to see the effect of that single variable.
assumptions: Abstract request-level model: no TCP, TLS, packets or real HTTP proxy semantics.
Each component has fixed concurrency slots and a FIFO queue; there is no CPU, memory or GC model.
Health probes bypass the request queue and answer instantly when the component is up.
Components do not know when their caller gave up; they finish the work and the answer is discarded.
Numbers are scenario inputs, not measured performance of any product.
expectedObservations: Requests still fail between the crash and detection, because two probes must fail first.
After detection, Server A carries all traffic and failures stop.
After recovery, Server B gets traffic again only after two successful probes.
